title: Year 12 Physics Module 6 – Electromagnetism
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Physics Module 6, organised by its four Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

categories.name: How do charges interact with electric or magnetic fields?

questions.prompt: What force acts on a charged particle placed in an electric field?
For a positive charge, is electric force in the same or opposite direction to the electric field?
For a negative charge, is electric force in the same or opposite direction to the electric field?
Must a charged particle be moving to experience a magnetic force?
When a charged particle moves perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field, what path can it follow?
Does a magnetic force on a moving charge change its speed when the force remains perpendicular to its motion?

categories.name: When is force produced on a current in a magnetic field?

questions.prompt: What effect describes the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
When is the magnetic force on a straight current-carrying conductor greatest?
questions.answer: When the conductor/current is perpendicular to the magnetic field.

questions.prompt: When is the magnetic force on a straight current-carrying conductor zero?
questions.answer: When the conductor/current is parallel to the magnetic field.

questions.prompt: Do parallel wires carrying current in the same direction attract or repel?
Do parallel wires carrying current in opposite directions attract or repel?
What rotational effect can a magnetic field produce on a current-carrying coil?

categories.name: How are electric and magnetic fields related?

questions.prompt: What quantity describes how much magnetic field passes through an area?
What law states that a changing magnetic flux induces an emf?
What law gives the direction of an induced current so that it opposes the change that produced it?
What device uses electromagnetic induction to change AC voltage?
Does a step-up transformer increase or decrease voltage?
Why is electrical energy transmitted at high voltage over long distances?
questions.answer: To reduce current and energy losses. Accept: reduce resistive losses.

categories.name: How is the Motor Effect applied to technology?

questions.prompt: What device converts electrical energy into mechanical rotational energy?
What component in a simple DC motor reverses the current every half-turn?
What stationary contacts supply current to the rotating commutator in a DC motor?
What device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
What induced voltage in a motor opposes the supplied voltage?
What braking method uses induced currents and magnetic fields without direct frictional contact?

finalRound.prompt: What law states that an induced current acts to oppose the change in magnetic flux that produced it?
